description: The shipped, historically-faithful preset: task T29's export of the classical-mediterranean ruleset. Every confirmed constant is the same figure toy-ruleset.json already carries (the same game), transcribed from the reports in the research repository's docs/reports/ and cross-checked here against the T04 fixtures corpus (tests/fixtures/corpus.json) wherever the corpus gives that constant its own id. _provenance.permilleScale: [designed]: the fixed-point denominator every AI personality parameter and every scoring ratio in this block is expressed in (parts per thousand). docs/design-audit.md §1 records the original's AI as out of scope for reverse-engineering by the project's own standing decision, so every number in this block is designed rather than decompiled; there is no original fixed-point convention to transcribe.
_provenance.defaultPersonalityPermille: [designed]: the value substituted for an AI seat's absent personality parameter -- the exact midpoint of the declared 0..1 range (permilleScale / 2), so an unset seat is neither a pacifist nor a warmonger. Searched docs/reports/ for an original per-nation AI default and found none: the original's TPickLeaders assigns a nation to a human or the computer and a leader name only, with no personality at all. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.maxActionsPerTurn: [designed]: the hard ceiling on commands one AI seat may place in one turn, checked before anything else, so a scoring bug that keeps re-proposing an accepted-but-inert command cannot hang a single turn forever. It binds occasionally on the shipped sixteen-nation classical scenario -- a 480-turn run of every seed 1-10 hit it 1-2 times each -- and AiTurnOutcome.HitActionCap reports every time it does. It never binds in the fifty-seed soak's own two-nation, three-city scenario, which AiSoakTests asserts directly (HitActionCap is false on every soak seed). The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision; this cap has no original analogue.
_provenance.minimumActionScore: [designed]: the score a candidate must reach to be worth placing at all -- one, not zero, so 'the AI did nothing this turn' always has one place to look; the gates, not this threshold, are what keep illegal or pointless actions out. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.besiegeCityBaseScore: [designed]: base score for besieging an adjacent enemy city -- the highest of the per-phase base scores, because taking a city is the only action that moves a nation toward the shipped totalConquest victory condition. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision; no original priority ordering between action kinds was found in the research reports.
_provenance.attackArmyBaseScore: [designed]: base score for attacking an adjacent enemy army -- below a siege, because destroying an army does not itself take ground, and above everything else, because it removes an opponent's ability to take ground back. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.attackFleetBaseScore: [designed]: base score for attacking an adjacent enemy fleet -- below a land attack, because on a world where cities are taken by armies a fleet is a means rather than an end, and because a naval battle's outcome is a sampled estimate rather than arithmetic. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.approachCityBaseScore: [designed]: base score for marching an army at an enemy city it is not yet adjacent to. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.sailAtFleetBaseScore: [designed]: base score for sailing a fleet at an enemy fleet -- below an army's march, because the objective is worth less (a fleet takes no ground), and above reinforcement, because a fleet has nothing else useful to do with its moves. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.reinforceCityBaseScore: [designed]: base score for marching an army at one of its own cities a hostile army stands next to. Kept below an approach so that an AI with nothing else to do advances rather than shuffling defensively forever. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.recruitBaseScore: [designed]: base score for placing a standing-recruitment order. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.mobilizeReadyRecruitBaseScore: [designed]: base score for mobilizing a fully ready standing-recruitment slot into an army unit, set above recruiting (the slot is already paid for and at its permanent quality) and below reinforcing (a besieged city's own defence still outranks a routine conversion elsewhere). Searched decompiled-mobilization-and-mercenary-restock.md for a stated original priority between mobilization and other AI actions and found none. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.fortifyBaseScore: [designed]: base score for ordering fortification at an owned city. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
_provenance.requiredAttackRatioAtZeroAggressionPermi: [designed]: the strength ratio, in permille, an attack must show at aggression = 0 -- 2.2 times the defender, chosen so a timid nation demands a margin large enough to survive the casualties a won battle still costs. docs/game-design.md §AI names the aggression/ratio threshold shape but not its value. _provenance.requiredAttackRatioAtFullAggressionPermi: [designed]: the strength ratio an attack must show at aggression = 1 -- 0.9 times the defender, so a fully aggressive nation attacks at a slight disadvantage but never a large one. The original's AI is out of scope by standing decision.
